steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light — particularly blue light — scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths like red and orange, spreading blue light in all directions across the sky. When you look anywhere in the sky (away from the sun), you see this scattered blue light, making the entire sky appear blue.
